text:
Lina: Proposal: instead of peering for every customer who needs source-ip preservation, we mint short-lived egress-binding tokens that agents in the customer VPC present to a lightweight egress-proxy we run in our regional relay. This lets us map requests to the customer's reserved NAT pool without full peering. Thoughts?
Devon: How would the token prevent someone from replaying it from another IP?
Lina: Token contains bound-client-ip and a sig, TTL short (30s), and a nonce. Proxy verifies sig and that source IP matches bound-client-ip. If mismatch -> drop or rate-limit.
Sam: Concern: trusting client-provided bound-client-ip for geo/fraud checks might be spoofable if the proxy sits behind NAT. Need TLS mutual auth/binding to connection.
Devon: We can bind token to TLS conn via a short-lived cert or use the TLS connection's src IP check. For customers where we run agent inside their VPC, agent can mint token for downstream requests it proxies.
Mike: Product question: which customers opt-in? Enterprises with geolocation/risk detection needs. Should be an opt-in feature for Private/Dedicated customers.
Lina: Agreed. Implementation sketch: agent in VPC requests token from customer-controlplane endpoint (or our controlplane for hosted) with HMAC using customer-managed key, receives token: base64(payload).signature. Payload includes tenant_id, allowed_egress_pool_id, bound_src_ip, exp, nonce.
Devon: Example token payload:
```
{"tenant":"acme","pool":"pool-123","src":"10.2.3.45","exp":1717801290,"nonce":"r4nd0m"}
```
signed -> base64(...).sig
```
// proxy verification pseudocode
payload, sig = split(token)
if !verify(sig, tenant_pubkey) -> reject
if now > payload.exp -> reject
if actual_src_ip != payload.src -> reject unless fallback-allow
route request using payload.pool
```
Sam: We should add a rate-limit and anomaly logging when src mismatch occurs. Also log token_id -> egress_ip mapping for audit.
Devon: Failure modes: if token is missing or expired, fallback to our regional relay NAT (loses source IP). We should surface metrics: token_minted, token_rejected, token_expired, fallback_use.
Lina: Rollout plan: 1) PoC in lab: agent mint + proxy verify in staging; 2) Canary with 2 customers; 3) GA opt-in. Need product + legal signoff for telemetry.
Mike: SLA/QoS: when using tokens we still need packet-level guarantees? Customers expect stable egress IP for allowlists. Token duration needs to be short for security but long enough to avoid chattiness. Thinking 60s for streaming-heavy customers, 30s default.
Sam: Also think about long-lived websocket/RTC flows where the source IP persists longer. Token approach needs rebind on connection reestablish or a separate persistent binding API for flows with long lifetime (with stricter auth).
Devon: Ops: proxy needs to cache tenant->pool mapping and keys for sig verify, rotated via controlplane push. Keep keys small and rotated every week by default.
Lina: Config knobs: token_ttl, allow_fallback boolean, mismatch_threshold for alerts, persistent_flow_mode toggle.
ops-bot: deploy-checklist created: https://internal/tasks/EGRESS-TOKEN-1 : add proxy verifier, agent mint endpoint, observability.
Mike: Product acceptance criteria: preserved IP in 99.9% of opt-in requests, <0.1% false-positives on signature verification, logs for every rejected binding.
Sam: Security checklist: threat model doc, key storage guidance (KMS/HSM), replay protection, token revocation path.
Devon: Implementation questions: do we want tokens signed by customer key or by our controlplane? Customer key gives stronger trust but requires customer KMS integration. Maybe start with our-signed tokens for Hosted and customer-signed for Private.
Lina: Good point. Phased: hosted -> our-signed, private/dedicated -> customer-signed (optional). Add a binding header X-Redwood-Egress-Token.
Devon: Small nit: TLS termination location matters. If we terminate TLS at regional relay, binding to TCP src IP still works. If we do SNI passthrough to upstream, we need to ensure we can still inspect token header for verification.
Lina: We'll standardize on terminating at the proxy for token path so we can authenticate. For flows requiring passthrough, fallback to peering or agent-side NAT.
Mike: Ok. Do we need a prototype before next architecture sync?
Lina: Yes. I'll own a quick PoC with Devon. Target: demo in 2 weeks.
Devon: I'll sketch the proxy verifier and a minimal agent mint endpoint.
Sam: I'll start a short threat model doc and telemetry spec.
Mike: Add me to the PoC channel.
Lina: Created #egress-token-poc. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
